items.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: we played in a jazz trio also for about a year where he played Hammond organ.

ctx.x: What was the big band experience? Where did that fit in as far as your career? Was it in the ‘60s?

Mostly in the studios because I hadn’t had any big band experience outside the studios at that time. And so the big band writers like Shorty Rodgers, Henry Mancini, Van Alexander, Billy May. Ernie Freeman did some big band stuff and he was also on some of the rock & roll stuff so actually he was really a classic writer, a very good arranger and stuff, but we played in a jazz trio also for about a year where he played Hammond organ.

Has the— I don’t want to say legal end of it — has the financial end of it changed for studio musicians at all from the late ‘50s until now? For instance if you play on a tune and it sells a lot of records —
